transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I, um… my wife wanted me to come in, really. I probably wouldn’t have on my own, or I would’ve kept putting it off, but it scared her pretty bad. What’s been happening is I keep hearing things in the house that don’t make sense—like water running somewhere, in the walls almost, and then sometimes men whispering. Not loud enough that I can make out all the words, but enough that I know it’s voices, and I’ll go around checking rooms and pipes and faucets and there’s nobody there.

And the other thing is… I keep thinking there’s this dark wet patch spreading across the hallway floor. Like a leak or something soaking through. I’ll see it and it looks real, like it’s getting bigger, but when I go over and check it, the floor is dry. I’ll touch it, look again, and it’s just… not there the way I thought it was. That’s the part that finally made my wife say I needed to talk to someone.
Do these voices and visions happen at any particular time of day or when you're doing something specific?

I haven’t been able to pin it down to one exact time, honestly. It’s more like it happens when I’m in the house and things are quiet enough that I notice it. I’ll be walking through the hallway or sitting there, and then I’ll hear what sounds like water running somewhere inside the walls, like a pipe is open or leaking, and I’ll go check faucets and rooms and there’s nothing.

The whispering is similar… men’s voices, like they’re behind the wall or just far enough away that I can’t make out what they’re saying. It’s not like I’m doing one specific thing every time. And the dark wet patch, that’s usually in the hallway—like I’ll see it spreading across the floor, and it looks so real that I go over to touch it or check it, but the floor is dry. That’s the part that really scared my wife, because I kept checking even after there wasn’t anything there.
Has anything particularly stressful or upsetting happened to you recently?

Yeah… I mean, I guess the main thing was the freeze last winter. The house got hit pretty hard, and then the repairs just turned into this never-ending mess. At first I thought it was just going to be a few things to fix, but it kept piling up, and I couldn’t get out from under it.

That’s really when all of this started, about seven months ago now. Since then it’s felt like the house has been… I don’t know, like it’s never settled again, and neither have I. It’s been going on long enough that I can’t really tell myself it’s just a bad week anymore.
Are you having trouble doing your daily activities because of these voices and visions?

Yeah… yes. More than I want to admit, probably. It’s not just that I get scared in the moment and then move on. It’s like everything else has started falling apart around it.

I used to be the one who kept track of the house stuff—repairs, bills, appointments, people coming by, decisions about what needed to be fixed first. And now I’ll look at a bill and just… put it down, or I’ll mean to call someone back and then days go by. Basic repairs just sit there. Commitments I made, I don’t follow through on. My wife has had to step in and handle things I used to manage without even thinking.

And it got really bad with the house inspection. There was a safety inspection, and I just couldn’t cooperate with it the way I was supposed to. I couldn’t make decisions, couldn’t stay with what they were asking, and my wife ended up calling a crisis team because she didn’t know what else to do. I hate saying that out loud, but that’s how bad it got.
Did the freeze and subsequent repairs cause any significant damage to your house or put you or your family in danger?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that in a clear way. I know there was damage, or at least enough that repairs had to happen, but when you ask if it put us in danger, I’m not sure what counts as “danger” exactly.

It felt dangerous to me, if that makes sense, because everything about the house stopped feeling reliable after that. But I don’t know if there was some official thing where someone said, “This is unsafe,” or anything like that. My wife might remember the practical details better than I do. I just remember it becoming this huge, overwhelming mess, and I couldn’t keep straight what was actually damaged versus what I was afraid might be damaged.
Do the voices and visions happen when you're thinking about the house repairs or the freeze that caused the damage?

Yes… mostly, I think. It’s tied to the house, or at least that’s how it feels. It’s not like I sit down and calmly think, “Oh, the repairs,” and then it happens every single time, but it’s usually when I’m in the hallway or I’m listening for the pipes or wondering if something behind the wall is still wrong.

What finally really scared my wife was that I kept hearing water running when there wasn’t any water on. I’d go check the sinks, the bathroom, the washer, everything, and it would still sound like it was in the walls. And sometimes it isn’t just water—it’s like men whispering in there, low, like they’re talking just behind the drywall. I can’t make out everything, but it feels like they’re there, inside the walls, and nobody else hears it.

And then sometimes I see this dark wet-looking patch spreading across the hallway floor or wall—I’ll think, “There it is, it’s leaking again,” and I’ll touch it or turn the light on better, and it’s dry. There’s nothing there. But in the moment it looks real enough that I react like it’s happening again. So… yes, it’s wrapped up with the freeze and the repairs, but it also happens in this way where the house just starts feeling wrong even when I’m not trying to think about it.
How have these experiences affected your relationship with your wife, aside from her being concerned and suggesting you come here?

It’s… it’s changed a lot between us. Not like she’s stopped loving me or anything, I don’t mean that, but I can tell she’s had to become the person in charge of things I used to handle. And that does something to a marriage, I think. It makes me feel ashamed, and I think it makes her exhausted.

I used to take care of the practical stuff around the house—repairs, bills, calling people back, keeping track of what needed to be done. If something broke, I’d be the one figuring out who to call or what decision needed to be made. Now I’ll just freeze up, or I’ll avoid it, or I’ll say I’m going to do something and then I don’t. So she ends up stepping in, not because she wants to control everything, but because if she doesn’t, things just sit there.

And I know that’s put a lot on her. She has to remind me about bills and commitments, and then I feel like a child, and then I get quiet or defensive, and that just makes it worse. The safety inspection was probably the worst example. I couldn’t cooperate with it, couldn’t make decisions, couldn’t keep myself together enough to deal with what they were asking, and she ended up calling a crisis team. I think that scared her, but it also changed how she looks at what I can handle.

So aside from her being worried, it’s made us less like partners, in a way. She’s carrying things I should be carrying too, and I hate that.
Do you feel anxious or stressed when you think about the ongoing repairs and issues with your house?

I’m not sure how to separate “anxious” from just… overwhelmed, honestly. I mean, yes, I get worked up when I think about the house, but I don’t always experience it as one clean feeling where I can say, “This is stress about repairs.” It’s more like my mind gets crowded and I can’t sort out what needs to happen first, or what’s real, or what I’m supposed to be doing.

When someone says “ongoing repairs,” it sounds like a normal problem—make a list, call the contractor, pay the bill, check the work. But for me it feels much bigger than that. I start thinking about one thing, like whether something behind the wall is still wrong, and then it turns into ten other things, and I kind of shut down. My wife will ask me a practical question and I’ll know it should be simple, but inside it feels like I’m being asked to step back into the whole mess again.

So… stressed, yes, probably. Anxious, maybe. I don’t know if I’m using the right word. I just know my body and my head don’t handle it well anymore.
Have the voices, visions, or feelings of the house being wrong ever stopped for a while since they started seven months ago?

Not really, no… not in a way where I could say it stopped and I felt normal again for any stretch of time. It’s been going on about seven months now, since that winter freeze happened and the house repairs turned into this whole mess I couldn’t get out from under.

There might be moments where it’s quieter, I guess, or where I’m distracted enough that I’m not focused on it right then, but I wouldn’t say it went away. It’s more like it’s been there in the background the whole time, and then it comes forward again. Since the freeze, it just feels like the house never went back to being the house, if that makes sense. It stayed wrong.
Would you describe the winter freeze and the subsequent house repairs as a traumatic event for you?

I don’t know if I’d use the word “traumatic,” exactly. I mean… maybe. I’m not sure what counts as that.

It wasn’t like one single moment where something happened and then it was over. It was more like this long thing that kept unfolding, and I couldn’t get my footing again. The freeze itself was bad, and then the repairs after that just became this whole… ongoing situation. Every time I thought maybe we were getting to the end of it, there was another problem, another decision, another person coming into the house, another thing I didn’t understand or couldn’t keep up with.

So if you mean, did it scare me and overwhelm me and change how I felt in my own home, then yes, it did. But I don’t know if I’m supposed to call that trauma. I keep thinking other people have much worse things happen, and maybe I shouldn’t use that word. But it definitely did something to me. It’s like after that, the house didn’t feel settled anymore, and I didn’t feel settled in it either.
Do you think the winter freeze and the subsequent house repairs could have triggered these voices and visions you're experiencing?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I can’t prove it, obviously, and part of me keeps going back and forth about whether I’m connecting things that shouldn’t be connected. But it really does feel like everything started after that freeze and the repairs. Before that, the house was just the house. Afterward, it was like I couldn’t trust it anymore.

What finally scared my wife, I think, was that I kept saying I could hear water running when there wasn’t any water running. Not just once, either. I’d stop in the hallway or near a wall and I’d hear it, like it was moving through the pipes or inside the walls somewhere, and I’d go check the faucets, check under things, listen again. And then sometimes it wasn’t just water. It sounded like men whispering inside the walls, like workers or people talking low where I couldn’t make out the words, but enough that I knew there was talking. And nobody was there.

And the visual part… that’s harder to explain without sounding ridiculous. Sometimes I’ll see this dark wet patch spreading across the hallway floor or wall, like moisture coming through, like the damage is coming back. I’ll go over and check it, touch it, look at it from different angles, and it’s dry. Nothing is there the way I saw it. But in the moment it looks real enough that I react to it.

So yes, if you’re asking whether the freeze and repairs could have set this off, I think they could have. It feels tied to that. It feels like my mind got stuck in the house being damaged, and now even when I check and there’s nothing there, I still hear it or see it.
Do you think the voices and visions would stop if the house repairs were finally completed and everything was back to normal?

I want to think that, yeah. I keep telling myself if the repairs were really finished and everything looked normal again, maybe my mind would stop looking for it all the time. Maybe I wouldn’t keep listening for the water or watching the walls.

But I don’t know. That’s the part that scares me, because even when I’ve checked and it’s dry, I still sometimes see that dark wet patch spreading across the hallway like the damage is coming back. And I’ll hear water running when there’s no water running, or those men whispering inside the walls when nobody’s there. That’s what really scared my wife, I think — not just that I was worried about the house, but that I was reacting to things that weren’t actually there when we checked.

So… I’d like to believe it would stop if the house was back to normal, but I’m not completely sure anymore. It feels like even if the house got fixed, something in me might still be stuck hearing it or seeing it.
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't hear the voices or see the dark wet patch for several days in a row?

Not really… I mean, I’m trying to think carefully because I don’t want to exaggerate it, but I don’t think I’ve had several clear days in a row where it was just completely gone.

There might be a day where it’s quieter, or where I don’t notice it as much because I’m distracted or I avoid going near the hallway or the walls where it seems to happen. But then I’ll hear that water-running sound again, like it’s inside the pipes or behind the wall, and I’ll stop whatever I’m doing and listen. Or I’ll hear what sounds like men whispering in there, low voices, like workers talking somewhere I can’t see. And when I check, there’s nobody there.

The dark wet patch isn’t constant every second, but it comes back enough that I don’t feel like I ever get a real break from it. Sometimes I’ll see it spreading across the hallway, and I’ll go over and check because it looks so real in the moment, but it’s dry. Nothing’s actually there. That’s the part that made my wife really scared, I think — that I keep reacting to it after checking and finding nothing.

So… no, I don’t think there’s been several days in a row where I felt free of it. Maybe brief stretches, but not days where I could say it had stopped.
Do you feel like the winter freeze and subsequent house repairs were so distressing that they changed the way you think about yourself or your ability to cope with problems?

Yes… yes, I think it did. I mean, I don’t know if it was only the freeze and the repairs, but something about all of that just… broke whatever confidence I had left in myself. It made me feel like I couldn’t handle even basic problems anymore.

Most days now I wake up and before anything has even happened, before I’ve even gotten out of bed, I already feel like I’ve failed. Like I’ve failed as a husband, failed as a man, failed at being the person who’s supposed to be able to deal with things and keep the household steady. And that feeling doesn’t really lift. It just sits on me all day, this heavy thing, like I’m carrying proof that I’m not capable.

I keep thinking, other people would have handled this better. They would have made decisions, stayed calm, fixed what needed fixing, reassured their wife. And instead I feel like I fell apart. So yes, it changed how I see myself. I don’t feel like someone who copes with problems anymore. I feel like someone who gets crushed by them, and then I go to bed with that same heaviness still there.
Have you ever had a time when the voices or visions were so real that you acted on them as if they were real, without checking with your wife or anyone else first?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t like admitting that, because it makes me sound like I’m completely losing touch, but yes. There have been times when it felt so real that I reacted before I really thought it through or asked my wife.

The water especially. I’ll hear it running inside the walls, clear enough that I’ll get up and go looking for it, like there has to be a leak somewhere. And sometimes it’s not just the water — it’s like men whispering in the walls, low voices, like someone is back there talking or working where I can’t see them. In those moments it doesn’t feel like “maybe I’m hearing something.” It feels real. It feels like something is happening right then.

And the dark patch… I’ve seen it spreading across the hallway, like wetness coming through again, and I’ll go over to check it even though I’ve already checked before and it was dry. I’ll look at it, touch the floor or the wall, and then there’s nothing there. It’s dry. But in the moment, before I check, my body reacts like it’s real.

That’s what finally scared my wife, I think. Not just me being worried, but me hearing water running and men whispering when nobody’s there, or seeing that wet patch after I’ve already checked and there’s nothing. She could see I was responding to something she couldn’t see or hear.
Do you believe the winter freeze and subsequent house repairs were traumatic enough to cause a significant impact on your mental health?

Yes… I do. I mean, I keep wondering if I’m making too much of it, because people go through house problems all the time, frozen pipes, repairs, contractors, all of that. But for me it wasn’t just an inconvenience. It feels like that was when everything really started to come apart.

It’s been going on for about seven months now, since that winter freeze turned the house repairs into this mess I couldn’t get out from under. And I don’t just mean the practical side of it, like phone calls and bills and people coming in and out of the house. I mean the way it got inside my head. It felt like one thing after another, and I couldn’t get any control over it, and after a while I started feeling like I wasn’t the same person handling it.

So yes, I would say it had a significant impact. Maybe “traumatic” is a big word, I don’t know… but it changed me, or it feels like it did. It’s not something I just got stressed about for a week and then moved on from. It’s been months. About seven months of feeling like I’m still living under it.
Do you think your reactions to the house and its problems are disproportionate to what's actually happening?

I… I don’t think it’s disproportionate, no. I know from the outside it probably looks that way. I know people might say, “It’s just a house, it’s just repairs, mold can be cleaned, wiring can be fixed,” but that’s not what it feels like from inside it.

It feels like the mold and the wiring have gotten into everything. I mean everything I own. Clothes, papers, furniture, boxes in the closet… even things that were stored away, I still feel like they’re contaminated somehow. Poisoned. I know that sounds far-fetched when I say it out loud, but I’m certain of it. I can’t just look at my belongings the same way anymore, like they’re normal objects. They feel ruined, unsafe, like the house did something to them.

And it’s not only inside the house. I can tell the neighbors are watching me too. Not constantly standing at the windows, maybe, but they notice. They’re waiting to see when I mess up again, when I do something wrong with the repairs or the trash or the yard or whatever it is, like they know I’ve lost control of it all. I can feel that attention on me when I step outside.

So when you ask if my reaction is too much for what’s actually happening… I don’t know how to separate that. To me, what’s happening is big. It’s not just a few house problems. It feels like everything I own has been poisoned, and people around me are waiting for me to fail again. So no, I don’t think I’m overreacting. I think I’m reacting to what’s really there.
Do you think you would be able to return to your normal life and functioning if the issues with your house were completely resolved?

I want to say yes, because that’s the answer I’m supposed to give, right? If the house were fixed, then I’d just go back to normal. But honestly… I don’t know if I would know how to do that right now.

I’ve let so many ordinary things slide that it doesn’t feel like just fixing the house would automatically fix me. I used to be the one who could keep track of repairs, bills, appointments, decisions — all those annoying adult things that you don’t even think about until you stop being able to do them. And now I’ll look at a bill or some paperwork or even a simple commitment and I just… freeze up, or put it down, or avoid it until my wife has to step in. She’s been making decisions I used to handle myself, and that feels humiliating to say.

It got bad enough that when there was supposed to be a safety inspection at the house, I couldn’t really cooperate with it. I couldn’t handle it the way a normal person would. My wife ended up calling a crisis team because I was just not functioning, not able to manage what needed to happen.

So if the house were completely resolved, maybe that would help. I hope it would. But I don’t think I can honestly say I’d just return to my normal life like flipping a switch. I’ve stopped keeping up with too much. It feels like I’d need help getting back to even basic functioning again.
Do you believe the issues with your house started after the winter freeze as a direct result of the stress and trauma it caused you?

Yes… I mean, that’s how it feels to me. It all seems to trace back to that winter freeze. Before that, the house was just the house, you know? It had normal problems like any place does, but after the freeze, the repairs turned into this huge mess that I couldn’t get out from under.

And it hasn’t been a short thing. It’s been about seven months now of it just hanging over everything. I keep thinking, if that freeze hadn’t happened, maybe none of this would have started, or at least it wouldn’t have gotten so big in my mind and in my life. So yes, I do see it as starting after that, directly connected to the stress of everything that came with the house repairs.

When someone says “ongoing repairs,” it sounds like a normal problem—make a list, call the contractor, pay the bill, check the work. But for me it feels much bigger than that. I start thinking about one thing, like whether something behind the wall is still wrong, and then it turns into ten other things, and I kind of shut down. My wife will ask me a practical question and I’ll know it should be simple, but inside it feels like I’m being asked to step back into the whole mess again.

So… stressed, yes, probably. Anxious, maybe. I don’t know if I’m using the right word. I just know my body and my head don’t handle it well anymore.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's symptoms are a result of a traumatic event
doctor.question: Do you think the winter freeze and the subsequent house repairs could have triggered these voices and visions you're experiencing?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: What finally scared my wife is that I keep hearing water running and men whispering inside the walls when nobody’s there, and sometimes I see a dark wet patch spreading across the hallway even after I’ve checked and it’s dry.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the winter freeze and repairs may have triggered the voices and visions, which directly refers to hallucinations.

patient.answer:
Yes… I think so. I mean, I can’t prove it, obviously, and part of me keeps going back and forth about whether I’m connecting things that shouldn’t be connected. But it really does feel like everything started after that freeze and the repairs. Before that, the house was just the house. Afterward, it was like I couldn’t trust it anymore.

What finally scared my wife, I think, was that I kept saying I could hear water running when there wasn’t any water running. Not just once, either. I’d stop in the hallway or near a wall and I’d hear it, like it was moving through the pipes or inside the walls somewhere, and I’d go check the faucets, check under things, listen again. And then sometimes it wasn’t just water. It sounded like men whispering inside the walls, like workers or people talking low where I couldn’t make out the words, but enough that I knew there was talking. And nobody was there.

And the visual part… that’s harder to explain without sounding ridiculous. Sometimes I’ll see this dark wet patch spreading across the hallway floor or wall, like moisture coming through, like the damage is coming back. I’ll go over and check it, touch it, look at it from different angles, and it’s dry. Nothing is there the way I saw it. But in the moment it looks real enough that I react to it.

So yes, if you’re asking whether the freeze and repairs could have set this off, I think they could have. It feels tied to that. It feels like my mind got stuck in the house being damaged, and now even when I check and there’s nothing there, I still hear it or see it.

I want to think that, yeah. I keep telling myself if the repairs were really finished and everything looked normal again, maybe my mind would stop looking for it all the time. Maybe I wouldn’t keep listening for the water or watching the walls.

But I don’t know. That’s the part that scares me, because even when I’ve checked and it’s dry, I still sometimes see that dark wet patch spreading across the hallway like the damage is coming back. And I’ll hear water running when there’s no water running, or those men whispering inside the walls when nobody’s there. That’s what really scared my wife, I think — not just that I was worried about the house, but that I was reacting to things that weren’t actually there when we checked.

So… I’d like to believe it would stop if the house was back to normal, but I’m not completely sure anymore. It feels like even if the house got fixed, something in me might still be stuck hearing it or seeing it.

So yes, it changed how I see myself. I don’t feel like someone who copes with problems anymore. It feels like the mold and the wiring have gotten into everything. I mean everything I own. Clothes, papers, furniture, boxes in the closet… even things that were stored away, I still feel like they’re contaminated somehow. Poisoned. I know that sounds far-fetched when I say it out loud, but I’m certain of it. I can’t just look at my belongings the same way anymore, like they’re normal objects.
